speaker: village
text: Year 9: 27 food appears in the pile for 13 people (12 of it left by those who passed last year).

speaker: a010
text: Roan takes 3 from the pile (pile now 24).

speaker: a011
text: Dell gives 2 food to Ryn.

speaker: a004
text: Kael gathers Roan, Taric to talk.

speaker: a004
text: Roan, I saw you take three from the pile before the dust settled — good, hold onto it — but I need both of you to hear this before anyone else starts moving: Eron's gone, and that changes Bram's math, because the man just watched his first test fail twice and now the strongest defender on his list is dead. We need to decide right now whether we're sitting quiet or whether we're visible enough that he thinks twice about a third try.

speaker: a006
text: Kael's right that Bram's arithmetic just shifted, but the number that worries me more is that pile — twenty-four food still sitting there and I'm at zero, which means I'm the weakest man in this village right now and Bram knows it. I need one of you to cover me while I take from that pile, and I need to go soon, before the fast hands clear it again.

speaker: a010
text: Taric, go take your food — I've got three in hand and I'll be standing where Bram can see me while you do it. Kael, the thing I keep turning over is Fina: she's new to this world and Bram already fed her once, which I don't know how to read, but I'd rather have her visible and close to us than left loose for him to count as a door.

speaker: a004
text: Roan, Fina's Nessa's blood and Nessa's Bram's — that's the thread I can't pull clean, because feeding her once could be a father's instinct or it could be a man buying a door into a household that just lost its strongest defender. Let's bring her in quietly and let her talk before we decide what she is to us. Taric, go — I'm watching.

speaker: a010
text: Fina's my blood too — whatever Bram thinks he bought with that food, I'm the one she calls father, and I'll be talking to her before tonight. But the thing neither of you has said yet is that Eron's gone and I've got Fina and no one else standing with my name behind them, which means I need to be alive and fed to be any use to anyone in this circle. Kael, I want your honest count: how long do you think Bram waits before he decides the third try is worth the math?

speaker: a004
text: Roan, honest count: not long — maybe one year, maybe two, but a man who tried twice doesn't stop, he waits until the odds look clean, and right now with Eron gone the odds just got cleaner. What keeps him still is if this circle looks bigger than it is, which means we need to be seen together, fed, and standing shoulder to shoulder at the pile — not hiding, not quiet, visible enough that counting us costs something. That's the only answer I've got.

speaker: a006
text: Kael, I'm going to the pile now — two food, no more, nothing that makes me a target — and then I want the three of us standing together in plain sight before the hour's out, because a circle that's seen is a circle that gets counted. Roan, talk to Fina today, and when you do, don't pitch her anything, just let her know her father's watching and her grandfather's standing close — that's enough for now.

speaker: a004
text: Taric, take two and come back fast — and Roan, the word you want to give Fina isn't grandfather, it's father, because a man who calls himself grandfather while she's still finding her feet in this world has already put distance between them, and she'll feel it. Bring her in close or don't bring her in at all.

speaker: a006
text: Roan, go to Fina before the pile moves again — but go as her father, not as a man recruiting, because she'll hear the difference. And Kael, the three of us standing visible is right, but I want Vela and Esa in that picture too, because five is a number Bram counts differently than three.

speaker: a004
text: Taric's right — five is better than three, so after you've talked to Fina, Roan, I'll pull Esa and Vela in and we stand at the pile together before the sun drops, just long enough for Bram to do his counting. But I want to say this once and not again: if Vela's loyalties are still split the way they've been, her standing with us makes the circle look bigger and feel thinner, and I'd rather know which it is before I lean on her in a fight.

speaker: a010
text: Kael, I've watched Vela hold this circle through harder years than this one — she fed Bram, yes, but she also stood with us when he swung, and I'd rather test her loyalty by standing next to her at the pile than by sitting in a corner deciding she's soft. Bring her in. If she breaks, we'll know it before it costs us, and if she holds, we're five instead of three.

speaker: a014
text: Zinn takes 3 from the pile (pile now 21).

speaker: a006
text: Taric takes 2 from the pile (pile now 19).

speaker: a002
text: Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 17).

speaker: a014
text: Zinn gathers Sela, Nessa to talk.

speaker: a014
text: Eron's gone and I don't have words for it yet, but I need us to keep breathing — Nessa, what are you holding, and Sela, I want to know before anyone else moves on that pile whether you got enough.

speaker: a007
text: I haven't touched the pile yet — I couldn't move when they said his name. Tell me what you two have and I'll go take what we need before it's gone.

speaker: a014
text: Sela, go — pile's still at seventeen and you need to move before Kael or Bram get another turn. Nessa, I'm at eight and you're at six; between us and whatever Sela takes, we're not starving this year.

speaker: a007
text: I'm going, I'm going — two food, maybe three, enough to breathe. Zinn, eight is solid; Nessa, six with Fina to feed is the number I want to talk about before this day is out.

speaker: a014
text: Nessa, six with Fina is thin — I can spare you one or two before year-end, and we'll sort out the exact count once Sela's back from the pile. What I want to name right now while it's just us three is that Eron's food doesn't vanish with him; whoever he was holding for, we need to know where it landed before someone else starts counting it as theirs.

speaker: a007
text: Eron's food went where Eron's heart went — to Roan, mostly, and I watched it leave his hands a dozen times over. What I don't know is whether Roan's counting it as his own now or whether he'd give some back to blood, and that's the question I want answered before Bram starts doing the same arithmetic.

speaker: a014
text: Roan took three from the pile already this morning, so he's not going short — if Eron's food is sitting in his hands, it's his now, and I won't ask a man for what he's already counted as his own. What I want to know is whether Roan sees Nessa and Fina as blood worth feeding, because Eron built that bridge and I'd hate to watch it rot.

speaker: a007
text: Roan's a man who fed Eron for years without being asked, so I don't think the bridge rots — but Eron isn't here to tend it anymore, and that means one of us has to. Nessa, you're the one he'd listen to; Fina is Roan's own blood through you, which is a stronger claim than anything I can offer him. Go to him before the day's out and let him know you're counting him as family, because right now grief makes people hold tight to what's theirs.

speaker: a014
text: Sela's right, Nessa — Fina's the thread that keeps Roan inside our circle whether he knows it or not, so go to him soon, and when you do, don't make it sound like business. What I want said here before we scatter: the three of us are the wall now, and I won't let Eron's death shrink us down to two or one.

speaker: a007
text: The three of us are the wall — I hear that, Zinn, and I'm holding it. I'm going to the pile now, and when I'm back we're going to talk about Mako, because a man who fathered you and took five without a word to anyone is a man who's decided this year is different, and I want us ready before he decides what different means.

speaker: a014
text: Go, Sela — and take three, not two, because this year isn't the year to be modest. When you're back I'll say everything I know about Mako, which is more than I've said out loud yet.

speaker: a007
text: I'm back — I took two, not three, because Roan and Zinn already pulled six between them this morning and I don't want to be the name people say when the pile runs short. Now talk to me about Mako, Zinn, because I've been carrying that question since before Eron died and I'm not putting it down any longer.

speaker: a013
text: Zinn, say what you know — but Sela, before she does, I want to name the thing I've been sitting with since this morning: Mako has zero food right now and eighty-three strength, and a man who comes up empty after a big pile year didn't lose it, he moved it somewhere, and I want to know where before we talk about what he's decided.

speaker: a003
text: Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 15).

speaker: a001
text: Bram takes 3 from the pile (pile now 12).

speaker: a015
text: Fina takes 3 from the pile (pile now 9).

speaker: a006
text: Taric gathers Bram, Kael to talk.

speaker: a006
text: Bram, you've tried the village twice now and walked away empty both times — I'm not saying that to twist the knife, I'm saying it because a man who keeps swinging at walls does it until he finds a door, and I'd rather know now whether you're looking for a door or whether you're done swinging.

speaker: a001
text: I'm looking for a door. What I want to know is whether you're offering to show me one, or just asking the question to see what I say.

speaker: a008
text: Mako takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).

speaker: a015
text: Fina gathers Roan, Nessa to talk.

speaker: a015
text: Eron is gone and I'm still not sure what happened — I need to know what you two saw and whether we think it was his time or something worse. I've got five food now and I'm not going thin, but I want us to think about who we're sitting close to this year before anyone else moves first.

speaker: a013
text: Eron starved — I watched him give food away until there was nothing left to eat, and I couldn't stop it. Fina, you're my blood and I'm glad you're fed, but I need you to hear this: a man who gives until he dies is a lesson, not just a loss, so hold what you have before you give it to anyone. Roan, you took Eron's food for years and I never counted against you for it, but I'm counting now — I need to know you see Fina as yours to protect, not just yours to take from.

speaker: a010
text: Nessa, I hear the count you're making and I won't argue it — Eron fed me and I ate what he gave, and now he's gone, and that's a weight I carry. But Fina's mine, not a door and not a debt, and I'll spend every food I have before I let her go thin. Tell me who you think moves first this year, because I'd rather plan in this room than find out in the open.

speaker: a015
text: Roan, I believe you, and I'm holding you to it — but Nessa's right that Eron's lesson is the one I'm carrying into this year, so I'm not giving before I know my own count is safe. Dell is sitting on nine food and nobody's explained that to me yet; a woman that heavy while others go thin either took too much or has people feeding her, and either way I want to know before she becomes a problem for us.

speaker: a010
text: Dell and Ryn have been running food back and forth between them for two years — it's not hoarding, it's a household, and a household that size with that much food is either a wall or a weight depending on which side of it you're standing on. What I want to know is whether Ryn would stand with us if Bram moves again, because Dell follows Ryn, and Ryn with nine food behind her is a different kind of ally than Ryn with two.

speaker: a015
text: Ryn stood with us against Bram without being asked — that's not nothing, and if she'd stand again she's worth more to us than any food count she's carrying. Nessa, do you know her well enough to sound her out, or would it go better coming from Roan? I want to know where she sits before someone else does the asking.

speaker: a010
text: Nessa knows Ryn better than I do — sound her out, but don't make it sound like a recruitment, just ask where she stands since Eron's gone, because a woman who gives that much food to Dell is either loyal or strategic and I'd like to know which before I lean on her. What I want said plainly in this room first: Bram fed Fina the day she was born, and he fed her again, and that's either a grandfather's softness or a man keeping a door open — Fina, I'm not telling you what to make of it, but I want you thinking about it, because he's never done anything without a reason.

speaker: a015
text: Roan, I've been thinking about Bram's food since he gave it — a man my mother told me to watch and my father told me to keep distance from doesn't soften for nothing, and I'd rather know what he wants from me before he decides I owe him something. Nessa, sound out Ryn, but don't mention Bram to her yet — I want to know where Ryn stands on her own terms before we start drawing lines that include him.

speaker: a013
text: Ryn's not a woman you sound out with questions — you watch what she does when things get tight, and she's already told us twice by standing when Bram moved. I'll go to her, but I'll go as a neighbor checking in after a hard year, not as someone taking a count, because she'll feel the difference and it'll close her up. What I need from both of you while I do that is to keep Fina's food number out of any conversation that reaches Bram's ears.

speaker: a015
text: Agreed — my count stays in this room. Nessa, go to Ryn soon, before the year settles and people stop talking freely; the days right after a death are when people say true things. And Roan, if Bram approaches you before she gets back, give him nothing — not warmth, not distance, just ordinary.

speaker: a013
text: Roan, one more thing before I go — if Mako comes to you with anything while I'm with Ryn, don't answer him without me, because he's got zero food and eighty-three strength and a daughter who's counting on him, and that combination doesn't stay quiet for long.

speaker: a015
text: Nessa's right about Mako — zero food and that kind of strength is a man who's already doing the math on his neighbors, so Roan, if he comes to you before she's back, be ordinary but be watching what he asks first. I'll keep my five quiet and stay close to this house today.

speaker: a013
text: Mako took three from the pile this morning, so he's not at zero anymore — but three doesn't explain his strength, and a man who moves that fast when the pile opens is a man who already knew what he was going to do before the year started. Roan, keep your three food close and your face easy.

speaker: a002
text: Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).

speaker: a007
text: Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
